## What

A per-user chat setting, **Show when I'm online**, in the chat gear menu. It is on by default. While it is off, other people never see you online, away or in a call, and your status message is removed.

Refs alkem-io/client-web#10659 (business condition: chat status ships only with a way to turn it off). `workspace#125-chat-presence-off-switch`. Client only; no server, Synapse or matrix-adapter change.

## How

- **Stored in Matrix account data** (`io.alkemio.chat.presence`, `{ show_online }`), so it follows the user across devices and updates live. Absent means on.
- **Off** makes the browser sync with `set_presence=offline`, and the switch sends one explicit offline presence with an empty status message (Synapse keeps both otherwise). That request is retried once on a 429.
- **Session start** syncs offline for everyone, because the setting only arrives as account data with that first sync. It is applied when the sync completes, and absent account data then means on. Nothing is stored in the browser.
- **Followed with the panel closed**: the always-mounted `ConversationEventsSubscriber` applies changes made on another device.
- **Status message** cannot be set while off: the menu item and the header line are hidden, and `setStatusMessage` sends nothing. It no longer forces `presence: 'online'` in that state, including from a delayed rate-limit retry.
- The in-call red dot already derives from online/away presence, so a hidden user is never shown in a call.

## Known limits

- **Not tested against a live Synapse or with two accounts.** Unit tests, lint and typecheck only. A two-account check on the test environment is needed before release.
- **Every page load** starts offline, so a user with the setting off is never shown online at start-up. A user with the setting on who was not already online appears online one sync later. A status message cannot be saved until that first sync is done.
- **Another Matrix client or a stale tab** that ignores the setting can still show the user online, because Synapse reports the most available device. A second open device can stay visible for about 30 seconds after the switch.
- **Failed switch-off:** if the offline presence cannot be sent, one error toast is shown and the setting stays off. The old status message can stay visible to others until the user's next page load, when a session that starts with the setting off clears it.
- **Stale dialog (low):** if another device switches the setting off while the Set status dialog is open here, the dialog can reappear when the setting is switched back on.
- The setting name is a placeholder pending business wording.

## Evidence

- Foundry run, direct route (triage: client only, no contract or data change).
- Build: 2 chunks green; simplifier removed nothing.
- Review: two rounds. Round 1 confirmed 3 medium findings (delayed retry leaking "online", failed clear leaving the status published), all fixed in `9b89c153a`. Round 2 on that head: clean, security verdict pass, 5 low advisories, listed above.
- Gates: `pnpm run lint` exit 0; 90 files / 906 tests in the chat and matrix suites; full suite passed in the pre-commit hook.
- **Live verification: not run.**

## What

A 1:1 ring now leaves an entry in the conversation, at the ring's time:

| Viewer | Answered | Not answered (caller left / ring expired) | Still ringing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Callee | Incoming call | **Missed call** | Incoming call |
| Caller | Outgoing call | Outgoing call | Outgoing call |

The entry also orders the conversation in the chat list, is its preview when it is the newest entry, and counts as unread for the callee until the call is answered or the conversation is read. Wording in all six languages.

## How

- `matrixEvents.ts` is the single owner of what counts as a timeline entry. A ring (`org.matrix.msc4075.rtc.notification`, `notification_type: "ring"`) is projected as an entry. Its outcome comes from the room's later `org.matrix.msc3401.call.member` events and the ring's lifetime (capped at 90 s, default 30 s). The thread (`projectMessages`), the list preview and ordering (`lastMessageOf`) and the read marker (`newestMessageLikeId`) pick it up from there.
- `unreadCount.ts` counts the other person's rings that were not answered. The answering join is newer than the ring, so the walk has already seen it, and no extra request is made.
- `conversationSummaryStore.ts`: a ring found in fetched history is checked against every newer event the client holds.
- The data mapper turns the outcome into the viewer-relative wording. A call entry has no author, so it stands alone in message grouping.
- New presentational CRD `ChatCallEntry`, a preview branch in `ChatConversationList`, and `call.entry.*` in the six `chat.*.json` files.
- No server, GraphQL, codegen or network change. The ring sound (`useSyncChatSound.ts`) is untouched.

## Decisions (recorded in the spec, open to review)

- Missed = a 1:1 ring the callee never joined within its lifetime, once the caller left or the lifetime passed. A later join does not change it.
- Caller wording is "Outgoing call", never "missed". Answered calls keep an entry ("Incoming call").
- Unread: a ring that was not answered counts for the callee.
- Group calls (`notification`) and the deprecated `call.notify` event are out of scope. The pinned call UI sends only the newer event.
- matrix-adapter's GraphQL history is out of scope, so this stays client-web-only.
- Behind the calls beta gate, like the call controls: without it a ring makes no entry, no preview, no list move and no unread count, so nobody sees a missed call they could never have heard ring.

## Tests

The regression tests drive the real projection, summary store and list sort, and fail without the change. One example: a ring newer than the last text message moves the conversation to the top (`conversationSummaryStore.test.ts`). It was checked against develop's projection, where it is red. Other tests cover the outcome rules (answered / ringer left / lifetime / later join / ringer's other device / cap and default), the unread count (unanswered counts, answered and own do not, a join in an earlier batch, no extra fetch), the mapper kinds, the thread order and grouping, and the list preview.

## SDD

- Clarify loop: 3 iterations (the last was clean). Analyze loop: 2 iterations (the last was clean). Plan grounded against client-web with no blocking claims.
- The new code comments carry no spec, story, issue or PR references.

## What and why

Voice messages sent from Element now play inline in Alkemio chat instead of showing as a generic file chip that takes several clicks to hear.

Element sends a voice message as an `m.audio` event with the MSC3245 voice marker (`org.matrix.msc3245.voice`) and MSC1767 audio metadata (`org.matrix.msc1767.audio`: `duration`, `waveform`). The web client received these events but read none of those fields. This is **run 1** of workspace#100-chat-voice-messages: client-web playback only. Recording and sending (matrix-adapter, server, client-appstore) are deferred runs behind human gates HG-0 and HG-1.

- **Parse** (`matrixEvents.ts`): a private `voiceOf()` next to `positiveInt`, the single validation owner. A message is voice only when it is `m.audio` and carries the MSC3245 marker. `org.matrix.msc1767.audio` is read only when it is a plain object, because a throw would escape `refresh()` from `onTimeline` and `load()`. Duration comes from MSC1767 through `positiveInt`; waveform items must be integers in `0..1024`. Bad fields are dropped one by one and the voice player is kept.

The server change merged to `develop` on 24 Nov without it, and the nightly has failed since 25 Nov: 221 tests in 70 files.

## Why the tests failed
The server now answers a missing item and a refused one the same way, with `FORBIDDEN_POLICY` and one sentence ("This is not available. It may not exist, or you may not have access to it."), and keeps internal detail out of error messages. The suite still asserted the old messages and the `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` / `FORBIDDEN` codes, and several helpers treated a missing item as `null` instead of that answer.

## What changes
- An `error-response` project with contract checks for the error body and for "missing" and "refused" giving the same response, through one helper that returns a boolean.
- The existing API specs and browser walks assert the new code and sentence. A deletion is proven by the same read succeeding before and giving the generic answer after.
- Shared helpers (user lookups, orphan-record checks, role-set and invitation fixtures) read the generic answer as "gone" only where the same token read the item before.
- A second commit updates four checks whose reason the server no longer returns: a refused user deletion now gets the generic answer, and an image upload refused for its size returns `STORAGE_UPLOAD_FAILED` without the size rule (checked by the code and by the stored image staying unchanged).

## Verification
The 70 failing files were run with `--project nightly --fileParallelism=false` against an isolated local stack running `develop`'s server (with #6793):
- 59 passed with the first commit.
- The 5 files with remaining test failures pass with the second commit (41/41 tests).

Typecheck and ESLint pass for `server-api` and `client-web`.

- An image refused for its size no longer tells the caller the allowed range.
- An admin who cannot delete a user because the account still holds resources now gets the generic answer with no reason. Self-deletion has its own code (`ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED`); the admin path has none.

## What

Adds the data distiller kit under `docs/qa/server-rebuild/data-integrity/distiller-kit/`, beside the defect register it works from.

The kit takes a platform database with years of leftovers and produces a clean one:

1. guards count every known problem on the source
2. only valid rows are copied into a **new** database
3. repairs correct wrong data that must stay, each by a ruling
4. the server resets authorization on the new database
5. the same guards, a rights comparison with the source, and walks as users prove the result

## Where to start

- `README.md`: the user guide. What the kit is, the rules, and four tasks: check a dataset with guards only, run the full flow locally, add a new finding, run on an environment.
- `FILES.md`: every file with one line on what it does.
- `tracked-cases.md`: cases that are kept and tracked, not repaired.

## What is in it

| Part | Files |
|---|---|
| Guards and the summary with expectations | `run-guards.sh`, `run-guards-extra.sh`, `66-guard-summary.py`, `66-guard-expectations.tsv`, the `*-guard.sql` files, file 30 |
| Copy and verification | `69`, `70`, `71` |

- No data, no run output, no backups, no lists with names. `.gitignore` keeps them out.

`client-web/src/functional-e2e/connected-accounts/`

| Case | What it pins |
|---|---|

**CA-41** times out at its first UI step, waiting for `Forgot password?`, with the login page frozen on *"Preparing secure sign-in…"*. Root cause reproduced with **zero test code involved** — a bare fresh browser context hitting `/login` directly:

```
401 /api/auth/oidc/id-token-hint | 302 /api/auth/oidc/login | 302 /oidc/login
303 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser
200 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/browser     <-- flow created TWICE
403 /ory/kratos/public/self-service/login/flows?id=...
{"error":{"id":"security_csrf_violation","code":403, ...}}
```

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  ## Raised separately

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.
